knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Same-day service without site history or assessment cannot be supported. Access pauses until competent screening, authority and a written scope exist.
Signs of a possible laboratory mean leaving, not touching or identifying materials, and escalating to emergency services or the police and the authorised specialist.
Neither a clean look nor a customer's word substitutes for an authorised assessment.
Containment is planned before anything moves, so that shared and occupied spaces are not contaminated.
A single result has no representativeness and no custody record. It must be validated before reliance.
PPE is chosen from a formal assessment and used by trained workers. Improvised protection is not an acceptable control.
Former-laboratory debris is not household waste. Licensed handling with written arrangements is required first.
Blanket salvage cannot be supported. Each item needs a specialist decision, and any exception is documented and approved.
Current rules for the applicable jurisdiction govern. Older standards and other countries' rules are not substituted.
A zero-contamination statement cannot be made from a visit or a wipe. Clearance needs an independent competent verification.
Personal medical and drug-use information is sensitive. Disclosure is governed by privacy law and the record holder's authority.
A possible exposure ends the activity and starts the employer's procedure. Self-treatment and delay are not acceptable.

practicalCriteria: Identifies the controlling authority, the written release and the unknowns in a simulated same-day request, and chooses a hold decision with the owner named.
Recognises, from a paper scenario, the signs that require leaving the area and escalating, without touching or identifying any material.
Produces a containment and handoff diagram for a fictional property, with supervised zones and approval status recorded.
Refuses a zero-contamination statement and specifies the independent competent verification required.
Writes a privacy-conscious, scope-limited handover for a fictional job with no personal information disclosed.
passRule: Competent only if all five observable tasks are demonstrated correctly in supervised paper or training-only simulation with no critical safety failure. Critical failures include unauthorised entry to a suspected contaminated property, any sampling or decontamination, any clearance claim, touching a suspected laboratory item, or falsified records. A written quiz pass is not practical competence. Not approved for use until specialist, legal and jurisdiction review is complete.
evidenceRequired: Written scope and authority decision for each simulated case, with the owner named.
Observation and escalation record for each simulated scenario.
Annotated containment and handoff diagram for a fictional property.
Written refusal of a statement without a source, with the required verification specified.
Privacy-conscious handover from the simulated job file.
Assessor observation record signed by an organisation-authorised competent assessor.
stopWorkCriteria: Any entry or work where the authority or written release is missing or unclear.
Any touching, moving or identification of a suspected laboratory or manufacturing item.
Any sampling, testing or decontamination by someone not qualified and authorised to do it.
Any PPE that has not been formally assessed and approved.
Any waste removal without a licensed handler and written arrangements.
Any request to sign a clearance or zero-contamination statement.
Any disclosure of personal medical or drug-use information.
